newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to hold special meeting on NATO.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to hold special meeting on NATO.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin will meet senior officials on Monday to discuss Russia's relations with NATO, the Kremlin press service said.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, presidential chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais and the foreign and defence ministers were due to attend.

A dispute between Moscow and the Western defence alliance over its plans to expand eastwards has become a prime issue for Yeltsin since he returned to the Kremlin last month following a heart bypass operation on November 5.
Yeltsin had talks with his friend, German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, on Saturday but they failed to bridge the gap between Moscow and the West over NATO enlargement plans.

"There is a well-known divergence in Russia's position on the one hand, and Germany and the other members of the North Atlantic alliance on the other on these issues (NATO expansion)," Yeltsin's press secretary, Sergei Yastrzhembsky told Interfax news agency on Monday.
"Boris Yeltsin clearly, precisely and fairly toughly laid out Russia's position and concern about the consequences of possible NATO expansion to the East."

Yeltsin is due to meet French President Jacques Chirac and British Prime Minister John Major soon, although dates for talks have not been announced. The dispute with NATO is likely to be one of the major items on the agenda at both meetings.

NATO foreign ministers are expected in July to issue invitations to some former Soviet bloc countries to join the alliance and offer Russia a role in shaping Europe's defence arrangements but no right to veto the alliance's expansion.
First in line are expected to be Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.
Moscow says NATO expansion plans are a threat to its security.
